title: New visual appearance
body:
I loved this app for studying but the new visual appearance looks AI-generated (some of the developers other apps are AI based).  So disappointing considering that Forest is partially about planting *real life* trees, yet the technology used to produce these apps are actively killing them. So do you care about money or the environment?
Many people I know who used forest have stopped due to the new interface, it’s so off-putting.
author: fixyourstupidadvertisements

title: Successive updates ruined it
body: I’ve used Forest for 7 years, but it’s really gone downhill in the last year. The pushing for plus interrupts use of the app, the most recent update has made the design cartoonish, obnoxious, and in your face, the time guard feature pushing itself on me when I don’t expect it means that I regularly have to close the app and restart after accidentally clicking on it, time crystals and coins are useless as new trees are all through events instead of buying them, the app doesn’t notify me when my trees have grown about 80% of the time.  It’s become a source of stress rather than a useful and aesthetically pleasing focus tool.

title: A Fantastic App!
body: The premise of this app is incredible. Growing virtual trees which keep you productive because of your conscience? Growing virtual trees that you can earn virtual coins with? Growing virtual trees that earn you virtual coins after which you can have a REAL tree planted? Once again, incredible. Would 12/10 download this app. Not only has it helped me stay focused, but I fulfil my inner plant nerd by getting to CHOOSE the type of plants I want in my garden. Not in the mood for a pine? Well, earn enough coins so you can buy that wisteria you've always wanted but could never afford because a) you're a broke student b) you can't afford a house which subsequently means c) you don't have land. Anyway, I'm rambling. Get this app. It's the best thing you'll do.

I would also suggest a new sound on their track shop: whale sounds. It's way more soothing than listening to traffic in Times Square or to café buzz in Paris.
